people_update.label: Donald Worster
people_update.identity_note: American environmental historian, b. 1941; Ph.D. Yale 1971; Hall Distinguished Professor of American History, University of Kansas, from 1989 until retirement; senior professor, Renmin University of China; former president of the ASEH. Wikidata Q1240502 confirmed by QLever on 2026-10-23 (the sheet's bulk match of 2026-09-22 is thereby reviewed).

proposed_edges.relationship: 'Gender and Environmental History' (1990) called his three levels 'a significant framework for research and writing in this emerging field' but found the essay 'lacks a gender analysis' and added 'a fourth analytical level, that of reproduction'
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Merchant's round-table response read in full (graph record pe131_merchant_jah_1990, pp. 1117–1121, author-hosted scan): the quoted phrases are already carried in donald_worster's description and scope note. Worster's essay is read in its 1993 reprint by search (graph record). Merchant's own entry is wave 2; this records Worster's reception.

proposed_edges.relationship: Agricultural capitalism as 'the decisive factor in this nation's use of nature' (Dust Bowl, 1979; 'The Dirty Thirties', 1986) and the West as 'a modern hydraulic society' (Rivers of Empire, 1985): the capitalist transformation of agriculture as the middle level of environmental history (1990)
proposed_edges.evidence_note: No new reading: the quotations stand as recorded in the graph's existing records (Dust Bowl at the page given by Cronon 1992; Rivers of Empire via Hennessey 1987; 'The Dirty Thirties' read in full; the 1990 essay in the 1993 reprint by search) and in the entry's description. Proposed so that the capitalism entry names the environmental historian who made capitalism an ecological category; the coordinator chooses the strand (none of capitalismdebates' eleven strands names him; origin_of_capitalism or transition_debate are the nearest). data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-environment.md P6.

proposed_edges.relationship: A history of ecological ideas, Nature's Economy (1977; 2nd ed. 1994), and the essays 'History as Natural History' and 'The Ecology of Order and Chaos' (1993): a reviewer of his last book recalled 'his wonderful knack for synthesizing complex ideas' in Nature's Economy
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Nature's Economy: graph record (1977, snippets). The Wealth of Nature contents read on OUP (data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-environment.md §8: 'History as Natural History', 'The Ecology of Order and Chaos'). Collomb 2017 para. 5 read in full. The 1994 second edition is not verified here. Target strand science/ideas.

proposed_edges.relationship: Named objections across a career: McDean on generalising the Dust Bowl region (1986); Collomb on Shrinking the Earth, 'very short on details about the human capacity for adaptation', its 'plea for an earth ethic almost rings hollow' (2017), while calling him 'the greatest US environmental historian'
proposed_edges.evidence_note: McDean 1986 (graph record, read); Cronon's 1992 reading is carried by p4C_rel_11, not here; Collomb 2017 read in full (paras 3, 12–14) and Gratale 2017 read in full ('a critical and important contribution', para. 11) (data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-environment.md §8). Source strands environment/dust_causal_debate and environment/anthropocene_climate.

proposed_edges.relationship: 'Transformations of the Earth' opens on Leopold's call for 'an ecological interpretation of history' and his Kentucky canebrakes (1990/1993), as 'Doing Environmental History' (1988) had grounded the three levels in the same call
proposed_edges.evidence_note: The chapter's abstract on OUP, which is its opening paragraph, read (data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-environment.md §8); the 1988 appendix read in reprint (graph record pe131_worster_ends_1988). Parallels edge_911 (leopold → environment), which cites the same texts.

proposed_edges.relationship: Braudel, Febvre and Le Roy Ladurie named as French sources of ideas for environmental history in the 1990 essay and its 1993 reprint
proposed_edges.evidence_note: No new reading: the names are as recorded in the graph's records for the 1990 essay and the 1993 reprint (read by search, 2026-10-13) and used by edge_111 (annales → environment). A person-level re-sourcing of that edge.

edges_considered_not_proposed.reason: A River Running West (2001) and A Passion for Nature (2008) are known by metadata only; no review was readable (MUSE and OUP blocked). Propose after a library read of Goetzmann (2001) or Harvey (2009).
Shrinking the Earth's world frame is a reviewer's gloss (Collomb); the body is unread.
His 1990 round-table reply to Cronon and White is unread.
